newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate reverses lows to end flat.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate reverses lows to end flat.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reversed mid-session falls to close unchanged at 22.50 percent on Monday after a late rush to sell paper, traders said.
"The (downside) pressure on rates seen this morning ran out of steam and those who wanted to sell low had to do so at higher levels," a trader said.
Overnight rates had reached a session low of 22.00 percent in midday trading, dealers said.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile up 50 basis points at 24.50 percent.
Another trader said market liquidity was ample despite overnight Cetes rates ending unchanged, due to company's filing tax returns for 1996.
"Banks may receive 70 percent of (company) tax payments and the Finance Ministry allows them to hold the money for about three days," which enhances liquidity in the system, the trader said.

Dealers said earlier falls in secondary market rates were also due to speculation ahead of Tuesday's primary auction of government securities, at which they predicted a fall of 50-75 basis points on bellwether 28-day Cetes.
Nonetheless, other traders said they though such falls unlikely as they could weaken the peso to levels of 8.10 per dollar.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed unchnaged at 7.9680/7.9720 per dollar.
Yields on 30-year Treasury bonds pared earlier losses, but were still off 6/32 to yield 6.96 percent when the Mexican money markets closed.
Banco de Mexico earlier drained 1.579 billion pesos through two auctions which it assigned at 24.27 and 24.81 percent.

Liquidity of 379 million pesos was scheduled to return to the market on Tuesday from prior central bank participation. Dealers said liquidity could however be under pressure from demand for cash prior to the forthcoming long weekend.
